source_caption:
More than just a superhero movie, Spider-Man 2 is one of the best stories ever told about responsibility and sacrifice.

Peter Parker is exhausted. He’s struggling with money, school, his relationship with Mary Jane, and the constant pressure of being Spider-Man. Every time he tries to have a normal life, someone needs Spider-Man again.

That’s what makes his story so relatable. Peter doesn’t want to be a hero because it’s easy. He keeps doing it because he knows that if he doesn’t, innocent people could get hurt.

The movie is filled with unforgettable moments, from the emotional “Spider-Man No More” scene to Aunt May’s beautiful speech about how heroes can inspire people to keep going. And then there’s the train sequence — one of the most iconic superhero scenes ever put on screen.

What makes Spider-Man 2 special is that Peter doesn’t have to defeat a villain to prove he’s a hero.

He has to choose between the life he wants and the responsibility he feels he can’t walk away from.

And he chooses to keep going.

That’s what makes Spider-Man such a timeless character.

source_details.title: Spider-Man 2
source_details.synopsis: Spider-Man 2 is a 2004 American superhero film directed by Sam Raimi and written by Alvin Sargent from a story conceived by Michael Chabon and the writing team of Alfred Gough and Miles Millar. Based on the Marvel Comics superhero Spider-Man, it is the second film in Raimi's Spider-Man trilogy (2002–2007), and the sequel to Spider-Man (2002). Tobey Maguire stars as Peter Parker / Spider-Man, alongside Kirsten Dunst, James Franco, Alfred Molina, Rosemary Harris, and Donna Murphy. The plot follows Peter Parker as he tries to manage his job, academics, personal life, and life as Spider-Man while also attempting to stop the scientist Dr. Otto Octavius from re-creating a dangerous experiment.
